label: Encrypt and decrypt a file for one recipient
prerequisites: Recipient public identity and independently trusted fingerprint
Recipient secret key and passphrase file, or hardware key reference and PIN file, for decryption
Supply a pinned trust policy to encrypt when revocation and expiry must be enforced
limitations: One recipient and native APG format only; bounded in-memory files
Encryption does not authenticate the sender
No forward secrecy against later recipient private-key compromise
Decryption remains available for recovery without trust policy enforcement
guidance: The envelope suite follows the recipient identity: X25519/ChaCha20-Poly1305 for apg-public-v1, P-384/AES-256-GCM for apg-public-p384-v1. Inspect discover limits before transferring data.

label: Sign and verify exact file bytes
prerequisites: Signer secret key and passphrase, or hardware key reference and PIN file, for signing
Public signer identity and independently trusted fingerprint for verification
Supply a pinned policy for revocation and expiry enforcement
limitations: Native detached APG signatures; no OpenPGP or platform code-signing compatibility
No confidentiality, trusted timestamp, replay prevention or automatic authorization
guidance: Verify against the expected signer and exact original bytes before consuming content.

label: Compute a SHA-256 file digest
prerequisites: An independently authenticated expected digest if using the result to detect malicious substitution
limitations: An unkeyed digest does not authenticate a sender
Not a password storage or password derivation interface
guidance: Compare digests for byte identity; use sign and verify when signer authentication is needed.

label: Create an identity and change its protective passphrase
prerequisites: Access-controlled passphrase file of 16..4096 bytes
New destinations; APG never overwrites files
Expected identity fingerprint when rewrapping
limitations: Rewrapping does not rotate the identity or invalidate old copies
Host filesystem permissions and secret-file cleanup remain caller responsibilities
guidance: APG internally derives a wrapping key with Argon2id and encrypts private seeds; no raw KDF endpoint is exposed.

label: Enroll identities and reconcile trust snapshots
prerequisites: Independently trusted identity fingerprints
Externally pinned snapshot digests and explicit approval of newly produced snapshots
limitations: Comparison and merge do not approve policy
No automatic revocation distribution or rollback protection; retain latest digest externally
guidance: Publish immutable snapshots and explicitly supply the approved pin to governed operations or MCP host configuration.

label: Revoke an identity and enforce the revocation
prerequisites: Identity private key and passphrase to self-revoke
Pinned public identity and trust snapshot to import the certificate
limitations: Certificate creation or verification alone does not enforce revocation
Existing ciphertext and signatures are not erased
guidance: Import the authenticated certificate into a new snapshot, then distribute and explicitly adopt its digest.

label: Constrain an identity to a signed validity window
prerequisites: Signer secret key and passphrase
Unix seconds with not_before strictly less than not_after
Pinned policy adopted by governed operations
limitations: trust.evaluate is advisory; caller-selected times never authorize execution
Enforcement uses the host clock
Validity imports can narrow existing windows only
guidance: Issue a signed window, import it into a snapshot, and apply that policy to encrypt, sign and verify.

label: Identify a native artifact and validate its structure
prerequisites: Bounded native APG artifact file
limitations: Inspection does not authenticate the artifact or trust embedded metadata
guidance: Use inspect to route an artifact, then explicitly invoke the appropriate authentication operation.

label: Exchange OpenPGP messages or GPG keys
prerequisites: A separately evaluated OpenPGP implementation
limitations: APG native envelopes, signatures and keys are not OpenPGP packets
guidance: Select an OpenPGP implementation for this application; APG has no compatible command.

label: Secure a live client-server connection
prerequisites: A separately evaluated TLS stack and peer authentication policy
limitations: APG file encryption is not a TLS handshake or record protocol
guidance: Use a complete transport protocol implementation; do not assemble a channel from APG file commands.

label: Store and verify user login passwords
prerequisites: A password hashing and verification implementation with application-specific resource policy
limitations: APG uses Argon2id internally but exposes no password verifier interface
APG hash is a fast file digest, not password hashing
guidance: Use a dedicated salted password verifier API; do not use APG hash or treat key wrapping as login verification.

label: Encrypt one shared envelope for multiple recipients
prerequisites: An implementation with an explicit multi-recipient format and policy
limitations: APG envelopes support exactly one recipient
guidance: Use a protocol implementation designed for multiple recipients; APG provides no group-envelope command.

label: Hybrid post-quantum encryption against future quantum attacks
prerequisites: Generate the recipient with key.generate identity apg-public-hybrid-v1
Recipient hybrid public identity and independently trusted fingerprint
limitations: Fingerprints and trust-snapshot digests use SHA-384; signatures are composite Ed25519 plus ML-DSA-65 (see quantum-resistant-signing)
Envelopes stay secure only while ML-KEM-768 or X25519 is unbroken; the combination has not had independent review
IronCrypto's ML-KEM is marked experimental upstream; APG checks it against PyCA and OpenSSL only
Software secret keys only; hardware identities have no post-quantum suite
guidance: Create a hybrid identity with apg key generate --identity apg-public-hybrid-v1. Encryption to that identity then always uses the hybrid envelope suite; there is no negotiation or fallback.

label: Require quantum-resistant signing
prerequisites: A hybrid identity from key.generate identity apg-public-hybrid-v1
The signer's hybrid public identity and independently trusted fingerprint
limitations: Composite ed25519-mldsa65 only; no SLH-DSA or standalone ML-DSA
Software keys only; PKCS#11, TPM and KMS identities sign with ECDSA P-384
IronCrypto's ML-DSA is marked experimental upstream; APG checks it against PyCA and OpenSSL
Signatures are about 3.4 KB and not interoperable with other composite-signature formats
guidance: Sign with a hybrid identity; every signature, revocation and validity certificate then requires both Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 to verify, so it stays unforgeable while either holds.

label: Keep private keys in a hardware token or HSM
prerequisites: PKCS#11: an apg build with the pkcs11 feature, host-set APG_PKCS11_MODULE, and a token supporting P-384 with CKM_EC_KEY_PAIR_GEN, CKM_ECDSA and CKM_ECDH1_DERIVE

TPM: an apg build with the tpm feature and a TPM 2.0 supporting P-384; on Linux also host-set APG_TPM_TCTI and an owner hierarchy with empty authorization, on Windows the Microsoft Platform Crypto Provider
PIN in an access-controlled file
limitations: P-384 identities only; APG never substitutes another curve
Tokens supporting CKD_SHA384_KDF and CKM_AES_GCM decrypt entirely in-token; others, TPMs and KMS release one per-envelope ECDH shared secret into process memory
Protection flags are self-reported token attributes, not vendor attestation; counterparties cannot see custody
The module runs inside the APG process with its privileges
No token PIN, object or policy administration
TPM key files are the only copy of the wrapped keys and load only in the originating TPM; tpm2-pkcs11 tokens lack ECDH and cannot decrypt through PKCS#11
guidance: Create the identity on a token with hardware.key.generate, bind vendor-generated keys with hardware.key.bind, or create TPM keys with tpm.key.generate; then use the resulting file as the key input. MCP hosts can add --key-custody hardware to refuse software keys.

label: Keep private keys in a cloud key management service
prerequisites: An apg build with the kms feature
Host AWS credentials allowed kms:GetPublicKey, kms:Sign and kms:DeriveSharedSecret
One ECC_NIST_P384 KEY_AGREEMENT key and one ECC_NIST_P384 SIGN_VERIFY key, created with infrastructure tooling
limitations: AWS KMS only; APG never creates KMS keys
SSO profiles need a current `aws sso login`; APG never refreshes SSO tokens
Every private-key operation is a billable network call to AWS
Decryption releases one per-envelope shared secret into process memory
guidance: Create the two KMS keys in infrastructure code, bind them with kms.key.bind, and use the resulting file as the key without passphrase_file. Set APG_KMS_FIPS=1 for FIPS endpoints. MCP hosts can add --key-custody non-exportable.

label: Require a FIPS-validated cryptographic module
prerequisites: Independent verification of the required module validation and exact deployment configuration
limitations: APG makes no FIPS validation claim
Outside in-token decryption, the envelope KDF and AES-GCM for hardware identities run in IronCrypto, which holds no CMVP certificate
guidance: Do not infer validation from an algorithm name; APG has no validated mode. Hardware identities keep private-key operations in the PKCS#11 module, whose own validation status and approved-mode configuration must be verified separately.
